days.title: Say sannu and hello
days.goal: Greet people in Hausa and say goodbye.

video.title: Must Watch — Fast way to Learn English and Hausa – Koyon Turanci

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of greetings: sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni, sai anjima out loud as you hear it.
Practise greetings: sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni, sai anjima aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.
Write down five of your own examples using greetings: sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni, sai anjima.
Record yourself practising greetings: sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni, sai anjima and listen back, fixing any mistakes you hear.
Use greetings: sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni, sai anjima in a real exchange today — with a friend, family member or language partner.
days.task: Say sannu, ina kwana, ina wuni and sai anjima out loud five times each.
days.challenge: Greet someone in Hausa today, even by message.

quiz.q: What does 'sannu' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Sannu' means hello. It is the most common Hausa greeting.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?

Name foods and say what you like.
Ask where a place is in Hausa.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Say sannu and hello — its goal is: Greet people in Hausa and say goodbye.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
